edits.text: 1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to requests to the extent they seek material protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or another applicable privilege or protection. Any request-specific objections and whether responsive materials are being withheld on those grounds will be stated in the individual responses.

2. PRODUCTION. Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control, subject to any objections stated in the individual responses and in accordance with applicable rules and court orders. The scope and timing of production will be specified in the individual responses.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent responsive materials are withheld on grounds of privilege or protection, Defendant will provide the information required by applicable rules and court orders to permit assessment of those claims without disclosing protected information.
4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement or correct these responses as required by applicable rules and court orders.

Before service, confirm the governing rules and orders, review each request, add request-specific responses and objections, identify whether responsive materials are withheld, and confirm production timing.

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We agree that the general framework alone is insufficient for agreement. We will provide complete request-specific responses identifying each objection, its basis, and whether and to what extent responsive materials are withheld before seeking your agreement. For scheduling discussion, we propose beginning production within 14 calendar days after service of those responses, completing production within 45 calendar days after service, and providing any required privilege log within 60 calendar days after service. These proposed deadlines remain subject to confirmation of collection feasibility and applicable orders; they are not yet confirmed production commitments. Undisputed responsive, nonprivileged materials will be produced without awaiting resolution of objections. The log will contain sufficient information to assess each privilege or protection claim without revealing protected information.

edits.text: 1. OBJECTIONS. Each individual response will identify any objection asserted to that request, its specific basis, and whether and to what extent responsive materials are being withheld on that basis. Any objection based on attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or another applicable privilege or protection will be identified in the applicable individual response. No general objection independently limits production.

2. PRODUCTION. Defendant will produce responsive, nonprivileged documents within its possession, custody, or control. Each individual response will identify the scope of production and any portion withheld based on a stated objection. Defendant will produce undisputed responsive, nonprivileged materials without awaiting resolution of objections to other materials. Proposed schedule, subject to confirmation before service and to applicable rules and court orders: production will begin no later than 14 calendar days after service of the complete request-specific responses and will be completed no later than 45 calendar days after service.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. For responsive materials withheld on grounds of privilege or protection, Defendant will provide any log required by applicable rules and court orders. The log will identify the applicable request, document date and type, author or sender, recipients and their relevant roles, a description of the subject matter sufficient to assess the claim without disclosing protected information, and the privilege or protection asserted and its basis. Any permitted categorical treatment or exclusion will be identified with its authority. Proposed deadline, subject to confirmation before service and to applicable rules and court orders: any required log will be provided no later than 60 calendar days after service of the complete request-specific responses.

NOT READY FOR SERVICE. Obtain the requests and complete each request-specific response after factual review. Confirm the proposed production and log deadlines with the client, collection team, and governing rules and orders; replace the proposed schedule with confirmed calendar dates before service. Do not represent these proposals as confirmed commitments.
